But behind them was not just a great poet.
It was a devotee who loved Rama throughout his entire life.
The story of Rama told by Sage Valmiki was already there.
Yet, Tulsidas presented the Rama he knew, the Rama he loved, in the common people's language of Awadhi as Ramcharitmanas.
Because he believed that Rama should not remain confined to scriptures alone,
His story must echo in every home.
His name must be on every tongue.
There must be a place for Him in every heart.
Through the story of Rama written by him,
Rama’s righteousness and his virtues became much closer to the people.
The love of Sita-Rama touched hearts.
Hanuman’s devotion became an inspiration for generations.
Lakshmana’s love and respect became even clearer to us.
That is why, every time we lovingly utter “Rama” in Ramcharitmanas and Hanuman Chalisa, let us also remember Tulsidas once, who carried that Rama-nama across generations.
🙏 On the occasion of Goswami Tulsidas Jayanti, let us remember him.
